context:
Goal: old claude-settings PRs whose work is done or dropped leave the list, and no wanted work is lost.
Problem (goal): the lane's test, "every change is elsewhere", counts work as covered when a replacing PR holds it, so it misses a replacing PR that was later closed without reaching main.
Based on (ruling): close-replaced-at-open, your Nov 9 21:27 CST ruling: a PR closes as replaced when the PR that replaces it opens, its branch is kept, and it reopens if the replacement is dropped; 12 old PRs are already closed under it (#1678, #1917, #1974, #2317, #1843, #1554, #1479, #1718, #2520, #1952, #1799, #1382).
Based on (notes): your 15:26 CST page note: what if PRs were intentionally closed without the work reaching main?
Departs from: main — the old PRs stay open; the lane closes the ones it finds covered.

options.gain: Nothing you still want is lost, the 12 closed under your ruling stay closed unless their replacement was dropped, and work dropped on purpose leaves the list too.
options.how: The lane closes an old PR when each change is on main, or a record says it was dropped on purpose, or its replacing PR is still open (your Nov 9 ruling). It checks the 12 already closed: one whose replacing PR closed without merging reopens. It saves each branch as an archive copy first, and lists the rest for you with what is missing. Undo: reopen.
options.label: On main, dropped on purpose, or replaced (Recommended)
options.lose: An old PR whose drop was never written down stays open until you look.

options.how: All 19 stay open until you look at them.
options.label: Leave all open
options.lose: 19 old PRs keep cluttering the list.

options.gain: You see every PR before it closes.
options.how: The lane lists all 19, each marked on main, dropped on purpose, or missing, and you choose per PR.
options.label: List each for you

ref: coordinator pick, Nov 12, 12:51 CST; reworded after your 15:26 CST note; corrected to keep ruling close-replaced-at-open
title: An old PR closes only when its work is on main or was dropped on purpose
why: A coordinator pick you could not see before.
